subject: Science
stem: The inner wall of the small intestine is covered with millions of tiny, finger-like projections that greatly increase its surface area for absorbing digested nutrients into the blood. These projections are called:
explanation: Villi (singular: villus) line the small intestine and dramatically increase surface area for nutrient absorption — alveoli serve gas exchange in the lungs and nephrons filter blood in the kidneys, both unrelated structures.

subject: Science
stem: Skeletal muscles (attached to bones, moving limbs) can be consciously controlled, unlike the muscles of the stomach or intestines, which contract automatically without conscious effort. Based on this distinction, skeletal muscles are classified as:
explanation: Skeletal muscles are voluntary (consciously controlled) — involuntary muscles (smooth muscles of internal organs, and cardiac muscle of the heart) work automatically without conscious control, even though cardiac muscle has its own unique striated-but-involuntary structure.

subject: Science
stem: Blood vessels that carry blood AWAY from the heart, typically under high pressure and (with one exception, the pulmonary artery) usually carrying oxygenated blood, are called:
explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure with thick, elastic walls — veins carry blood back TO the heart under lower pressure and have valves to prevent backflow; capillaries are the tiny vessels where actual exchange with tissues occurs.
